title: Self-Attention to Operator Learning-based 3D-IC Thermal Simulation
problem: Efficient thermal simulation for 3D ICs with high power densities; traditional PDE-solving methods are accurate but computationally slow for iterative design workflows.
motivation: 3D IC thermal management is increasingly critical as power densities rise; existing ML approaches like Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) sacrifice high-frequency information fidelity and require extensive high-quality training data.
method: The approach uses a neural network called SAU-FNO (Self-Attention UNet Fourier Neural Operator) that learns to predict how heat flows through 3D chips. It combines three complementary techniques: self-attention (which lets the network track how temperature changes in one part of the chip affect distant regions), U-Net architecture (which processes thermal features at multiple scales simultaneously), and Fourier Neural Operators (which efficiently model both fine-grained temperature details and broader heat patterns). To train this network efficiently, the method uses transfer learning: it starts with low-fidelity simulations (fast but less precise) and fine-tunes on high-fidelity data (slow but accurate), which reduces the need for expensive high-fidelity training data.
key_novelty: The hybrid architecture combines self-attention (which captures thermal interactions across the chip), U-Net (which preserves fine temperature details), and Fourier Neural Operators (which model heat patterns) to capture both high-frequency temperature information and long-range thermal dependencies, trained efficiently via transfer learning using low-fidelity simulation data.
contributions: SAU-FNO architecture integrating self-attention and U-Net with FNO for improved thermal modeling
Transfer learning approach enabling training with low-fidelity data
primary_theme: ML-based 3D IC thermal simulation via self-attention FNO and transfer learning
